chunks: Uthman ibn Isa from Ali ibn Salm who said, 'I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say,'

Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, said, 'I am the most needless of all who are needless of a partner, so whoever ascribes to Me another as a partner in any action he undertakes, I will not accept it from him. And I do not accept anything but that which was done only for Me exclusively.'

key_terms.الشَّرِيكِ: The partner; one who shares authority or credit
key_terms.الْأَغْنِيَاءِ: The self-sufficient ones; here referring to God's absolute needlessness
key_terms.خَالِصًا: Pure/exclusive; done solely for God without any shirk or show-off

ai.seo_question: What does God say about accepting deeds performed with partners?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd* highlights the Divine Speech (Qawl Allah) where God declares His self-sufficiency, rejecting any deed performed with a partner other than Him. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *ikhlas* (purity of intention), noting that even acts of worship are void if mixed with *riya'* (showing off) or self-admiration. The narration serves as a foundational text for understanding the spiritual condition of acceptance, linking internal sincerity directly to divine approval.
